## Design decisions

### Memory (full set, with mipmaps; `src/core/sets.ts` counts w*h*4*4/3 for any image)

- Surface wrap 8192 x 4096: 171 MB. Cloud RGBA 8192 x 4096: 171. Emissive 4096 x 2048: 43. Storm mask 2048 x 1024: 11. Patches 5 x 4096 squared: 427 (96, 48, 24, 12, 6 degrees; nadir at altitude 0.03 needs a patch at most 7.2 degrees wide; confirm with G13). Relief about 350. Sky patches about 200. Moon about 15. Total about 1390 of 1400. Web set is a quarter. No height map for the globe.

### Layers of the globe

- Surface S (cloud free) and a cloud layer (color W, alpha a), composed in linear albedo: A = (1-a) S shadow + a W, then times the light curve.
- Solved from the hero: a = max over channels of (C - S~)/(Wmax - S~) against the declouded estimate S~ (Seedream take, low frequencies matched on clear areas, its bright glint patch on the Pacific west of Mexico flattened). Where a is under a threshold S = hero and a = 0. Elsewhere W = (C - (1-a) S~)/a, so the hold midpoint gives the hero back exactly.
- Cloud shadows: shader samples the cloud alpha offset toward the Sun (h tan zenith), soft. The surface is divided by the mid-hold shadow so the hero still matches.
- Cloud drift about the axis as a closed form d(t) that runs in the hold and eases to 0 by about 0.5 s after the hold ends, then stays 0, so the patches bake clouds at state 0 with no jump. The mid-hold offset is a whole number of map pixels (for example 12 px = 0.527 degrees, about 0.21 degrees per second) and the hero clouds are unprojected through the mid-hold warp. The hurricane turns the same way (storm mask as on Mars, counterclockwise, frozen at 0 after the hold; the unprojection includes the mid-hold angle). The hold orbit direction opposes the spin.
- Emissive map (RGBA, alpha says aurora): city lights (warm, twinkle) and on-disc aurora (green, ripple), taken from the hero night side and removed from the surface; far-side lights from Black Marble restyled by code; fade in past the terminator.
- Off-limb aurora: a shell raymarch (radius 1.0 to about 1.09) from a footprint map with ray structure, green low and red high, rippling, fitted by eye to the hero. Aurora, Moon and limb glow are removed from the hero sky patch.
- Light curve measured from the hero (white cloud envelope and ocean per sun-angle bin, 33 knots as `uCurve`). Haze shells (`src/bodies/haze.ts`, parameters as in `src/stops/mars/haze.json`) fitted by my own script to hero limb profiles; grazing layer across the disc edge on the lit and the night side.
- Hero pixels (from the 2x copy) where the view cosine is above 0.42, fading to 0.2. The rest is painted from the Blue Marble guide warped to the hero layout (thin plate spline on landmarks) and repainted in the hero style in gnomonic tiles with flow checks. Poles on a polar projection. Far-side clouds are a generated cloud layer.
- Moon: sphere with its own painted map plus hero pixels as a lit overlay (`src/bodies/moonbody.ts` pattern), moving along its orbit.

### Terrain

- Geography: camera over the Caribbean south of Cuba (about lon -81, lat 19) looking north. Long island = Cuba, peninsula = Florida, banks = Bahamas. The globe Sun is WNW of the spot while the close image has the Sun ahead; the cover hides that.
- A predictor (the hero globe rendered from the terrain camera pose) chooses the spot and the heading. The patch chain is strict super-resolution of the hero composite with clouds baked in; the cloud layer is off where a patch has full weight.

### Stop code

- Own copy of the planet shader in `src/stops/earth/` (mesh quaternion from the fit, `EQUIRECT_GLSL`, patches via gnomonic `uSpotN/E/U`, fade by parent texel density `[1.02, 1.5]`, feather 0.12). `set.ts` follows `src/stops/mars/set.ts` (orbit and terrain groups, descent grade by altitude 0.7 to 0.05 radii, sky patches from `sky.json`, `Relief.load`), plus `look.ts`, `assets.ts`, `plan.ts`.

## Pipeline as built (03:00 to 03:40 UTC)

All scripts in `assets-src/earth/`, work files in `out/work/earth/` (not in git). Order: `light.py` (curve and disc haze), `split.py` (layers of the hero), `motion.py` (imported), `wrap.py 8192` (maps, full and web).

- `light.py`: writes `src/stops/earth/curve.json` (33 knots), `assets-src/earth/limbhaze.json` and `src/stops/earth/limb.json`. Disc haze model, the same in `geo.limb_haze` and in `globe.ts`: `T = exp(-depth exp(-(mu/width)^power))`, in-scatter `(pale (shadeG/2)^gamma ramp(dayFrom, dayTo, ndl) + night)(1 - T)`. First fit had per-channel depth [0.55, 5.63, 6.76] with red pale at its bound: the render showed a red-brown rim on the night limb (red passed through). Refit 03:38 with one depth for all channels: pale [0.5448, 1.3654, 2.1529], depth 3.5289, width 0.05, power 0.5941, gamma 0.7438, rms log 0.299. Night limb term [0.0066, 0.0246, 0.0406] (measured inside the night limb).
- `split.py` (hero at 2x, 3168 x 5632): writes `out/work/earth/split/{surface,cloud,alpha,hero-albedo,city,aurora,shadow,haze}.npy`. A0 0.02, A1 0.12, cloud colour (0.86, 0.88, 0.9), shadow height 0.006 strength 0.4 blur 5 even 14. City gate: 17 px top-hat, warm chroma, night ramp `geo.NIGHT = (0.04, -0.14)`, inpaint under lights. Aurora gate with zone. Haze subtraction protected by a local floor (0.8 of eroded luminance). Recompose error against the hero: mean 0.208, p99 2.705, max 78.8 code values. Cloud cover 0.348, thick 0.256. About 90 s.
- `motion.py` and `src/stops/earth/motion.json`: drift 0.4 deg/s with profile -cos(3 lat) (tropics westward), ease 0.5; s(t) = -x^2/(x + 0.5), x = holdEnd - t, 0 after the hold; S_MID = -2.0833. Storm centre lon -106.154, lat 17.368 (hero px 1085, 730), 5 deg/s at the centre, core 6 deg, fade 10 to 16 deg, counterclockwise (arms trail; checked in the hero). `warp = drift(twist)`, `unwarp` is the exact inverse (roundtrip 2e-16). Shadow height 0.006, strength 0.4, lod 2.5, floor 0.12. Emissive peak 5.
- `wrap.py`: azimuthal equidistant registration (12 px per degree, radius 120 deg, centre lon -77.354 lat 13.777) of the July Blue Marble to the hero by dense flow on blueness, smoothed, faded outside. Measured flow median 4.94 deg, p95 11.3, max 14.7 (`out/work/earth/view/reg-check-crop.jpg`): the hero geography is distorted against the real Earth, so every real guide goes through `real_dirs(y, flow)`. Far-side colour: 32 cubed LUT from registered pairs (Blue Marble colour to hero surface albedo). Hero weight smoothstep(0.2, 0.42, view cosine). Cloud map: hero clouds through `motion.unwarp(y, S_MID)`, far clouds from VIIRS whiteness; WebP saved with `exact=True` (keeps colour under zero alpha). Emissive RGBA: RGB = city / max(night factor, 0.2) / peak, sRGB coded; A = sqrt(aurora / max(gate, 0.25) / peak). Writes `src/stops/earth/wrap.json`. Caches in `out/work/earth/guide/` (`flow.npy`, `lut.npy`): delete to rebuild. About 2 minutes.
- Guides in `references/cache/earth/`: `bluemarble-july-21600.jpg`, `viirs-2020-09-10.jpg`, `blackmarble-13500.jpg`, plus the two smaller first fetches. Rows in ASSETS-ROWS.md.

## Stop code as built

- `globe.ts` (`Globe`): own copy of the planet shader, no height map. Surface (filmic coded), patch chain (gnomonic; `baked` weight turns the live cloud layer off), cloud RGBA at `cloudDir(d)` (twist about the storm axis, then drift; `uFlow` = s), shadow = cloud alpha at `normalize(d + (sun - d ndl) h / max(ndl, floor))` by `textureLod`, light curve `uCurve[33]`, disc haze, emissive city lights with twinkle and aurora (alpha squared, colour (0.22, 1, 0.42)) with ripple, both equal to the hero at mid hold (`uClock` = time - holdMid). `diagOut`, alpha 1. GLSL reserved words bite: `cast` is one.
- `air.ts` (`Air`): BackSide sphere radius 1 + 0.3, blending (ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA; alpha ZERO, ONE), depthTest off. Outside the disc three exponentials in tangent height times a day factor about `uGlowDir`, plus a night term; inside the disc a band exp(h / inner) toward the rim colour. `uWide` scales the two wide layers with descent. `air.json` is a first guess, to be fitted by `air.py`.
- `set.ts`: globe + air + `FarPoint`; light = `plan.lightDir` rotated by `state.rotation`; `low` descent factor between altitude 0.7 and 0.05; `sky: []`; no Moon; terrain is still the stand-in plate (`standin-close.jpg`).

## Orbit view, second pass (03:40 to 04:20 UTC)

### Findings

- The hero disc is an ellipse, not the fitted circle: limb deviation from -12 px (position angle 12 to 30) to +3 px (290). `shape.py` fits an ellipsoid in the camera frame (s1 1.00556, s2 0.98955, long axis at position angle 106, view axis sqrt(s1 s2)); lit limb rms 1.13 px, max 5.0. It writes `src/stops/earth/shape.json` (`matrix`). `geo.py` has `SHAPE`, `SHAPE_INV`, a `Shaped` body; `hero_geometry` returns `rt` (tangent distance in the unit-sphere space, 1 at the limb) and `at` (unit vector to the tangent point). In `set.ts` a `shape` group carries the matrix; globe, air and aurora are its children. The eye is brought into that space for the shaders.
- Position angle convention everywhere: pa = atan2(px - cx, -(py - cy)), 0 up, 90 right, 180 down, 270 left. Lit limb about pa 200 to 20, night limb pa 80 to 190, aurora curtains pa 14 to 78. Fit camera quaternion is identity, so world x, y are image right, up.
- GLSL: `cast` is a reserved word.
- The image `read` tool often fails once right after a file is written. Retry.

### Air (`air.py`, `air.ts`, `air.json`, `air-glow.png`)

- Samples: median of hero minus sky fill minus offset (0.0021, 0.0026, -0.0008) per 4 degree sector and height bin, aurora sector and Moon masked. Four exponential layers times a day factor x = (dot(at, dir) + 1) / 2 raised to a power per layer. Fit: heights [0.012, 0.012, 0.0526, 0.5], powers [0.3, 4.08, 3.5, 1.0], dir [-0.9016, 0.3311, 0.2784], rms log 0.32. Angular lumps of about 40 percent remain, so a ratio map (180 x 64, u = position angle, v = sqrt(h / 0.6), RGB = ratio / 4, A = line ratio / 4) corrects the layers at the hold; `uPhysical` fades it to 1 with descent and after the hold. Rows 64 to 71 of the same PNG hold the rim colour per position angle (hero median 2.7 to 7.5 px inside the limb, sqrt coded, times 4).
- Blue limb line: Gaussian of width 0.0016 radii centred at h = -0.0009 (measured peak at -0.0011), colour (0.496, 1.789, 4.195) times x^4.31 times the line ratio.
- Inner band: cover = 0.92 exp(h / 0.007) toward the rim colour from the map (hold) or mix(rimNight, rim, smoothstep(0.42, 0.68, x)) (physical). The first version used x^0.5 as the day factor and drew a pale line round the night limb: fixed.
- `limbcheck.py STILL pa...` prints hero and film radial profiles across the limb (scene linear). Run it on `npm run still -- --frame 1755 --tier draft --out FILE`.
- Measured after the fix: lit limb pa 250 film within about 10 percent of the hero from +2 px outward; night limb pa 160 film (0.013, 0.026, 0.040) against hero (0.007, 0.014, 0.021) just inside (still a little bright); inside the lit limb the wrap content differs from the hero (far side painting starts at view cosine 0.42).

### Moon (`moon.py`, `moon.ts`, `moon.json`)

- Limb circle fitted on the lit arc of the 2x hero by steepest radial descent: centre shifted (+3.9, +1.05) px at 1x from the fit, radius 58.1 px (fit said 52.5). World centre [22.016856, 11.301699, -54.685321], radius 1.16755.
- Maps 1024 x 512 (web 512 x 256): `moon-color.jpg` (albedo from the lit hero pixels, mirrored to fill, flat grey elsewhere, coded times 0.4) and `moon-lit.webp` (hero pixels with their light baked, alpha = front mask). Shader: albedo times sun colour times (smoothstep terminator times ndl^0.55) plus earthshine, mixed to the baked pixels by the mask. Motion as Mars: home rotated about `plan.axis` by `moonDegPerSecond` times (time - holdMid).

### Sky patch (`sky/patch.py`, `sky.json`)

- `sky.json` gain is 1 / skyExposure = 2.380952 (plan has skyExposure 0.42). To render the film with a black sky set that gain to 0 for one still (`out/work/earth/still/hold-nosky.png`, review tier), then `python3 assets-src/earth/sky/patch.py out/work/earth/still/hold-nosky.png`.

## Terrain view as built (04:55 to 05:50 UTC)

The older "Terrain" design above (spot at lon -81, lat 19, patches with baked clouds) is replaced by this.

### Scripts, in order (`assets-src/earth/relief/`, work files in `out/work/earth/relief/`)

1. `camfit.py`: camera of the close image at vfov 45. Result `camera-fit.json`: pitch 28.348 degrees down, altitude 0.030751 radii, sphere radius 32.5197 camera heights, nadir [0.030783, -0.879541, -0.474826], horizon dip 14.03, roll -2.0. `geom.py` has the rays, the sea sphere and `horizon_row`.
2. Margins (asset "relief margin", 6 of 6 takes used this round): the image is outpainted to a canvas 4096 x 1980 at 1x (640 px left and right, 396 px below). `marginfit.py`, `edgefit.py`, `margincomp.py`, `cornercomp.py` align the takes to the image and compose strips; strips and the close image are upscaled x2 (`tools/ml/upscale.py`). Prompts in `margin-prompt-*.txt`.
3. Clean plate (asset "relief plate", take 1 kept): `nano_banana_pro` on `references/approved/earth-close.jpg`, prompt `plate-prompt.txt`, the thunderheads and their shadows painted out. `platefit.py t1` aligns it (ECC 0.9997, affine [[1.0001, 0, -0.2987], [0, 1.0079, -6.1258]], flow where unchanged median 0.20 px) and corrects a low-frequency colour offset. Fine texture is regenerated everywhere in the plate, so it is used only beneath the towers.
4. Matte (asset "relief matte", take 1 kept): same tool and input, prompt `matte-prompt.txt`, white towers on black, aligned with the plate's affine. GrabCut and difference thresholds were tried first and rejected.
5. `build.py`: everything that ships. Towers = matte components of 300 px and more, groups = components of the matte dilated 13 px, a base line per group, lift = 0.5 (1 - reach(base) / reach(pixel)) above the base and 0 below, capped at 0.085 (a 16 km tower seen from 196 km), alpha = matte dilated 2 px and blurred 1.2. Ground beneath the towers = clean plate plus a membrane (Laplace solve of image minus plate from 10 px outside the matte) blended in from 10 to 6 px, then limited so the tower layer stays above zero. Tower colour is premultiplied in scene linear: image minus (1 - alpha) ground. Layers put together give the image back: mean abs 0.003, max 4 code values. Above the horizon the ground texture holds air minus sky (sky = running minimum from the top of the star-free image, saved as `sky-target-1x.npy`), so the limb glow rides with the ground and the sky comes from the sky patch. Masks at a quarter of the canvas: R glint, G drift weight (off on land and banks, hand polygon `LAND`).
   - Outputs in both sets: `relief-ground.webp` (full 8192 x 3960 lossless 21.3 MB, web 4096 x 1980 1.3 MB), `relief-towers.webp` (RGBA, full 5616 x 2432 1.6 MB), `relief-lift.bin` (float32, 1404 x 608), `relief-masks.png`; `src/stops/earth/relief.json`.
   - `towers.py` is the rejected difference-threshold attempt (to delete).

### Code

- `relief.ts` (`Ground`): ground mesh on the sea sphere of the fitted camera, alpha = smoothstep across the fitted horizon polynomial, colour added above it. Towers mesh at distance sea x (1 - lift), premultiplied, no depth test. Drift `look.ground.drift` [-3.2, 0.1] px per second times masks.g and shimmer [0.3, 220, 1.6, 0] times masks.r, both zero at the judged frame (`ground.update(state.time - terrainMid, ...)`).

## Dive and rise (from 06:00 UTC)

### Engine facts (`src/director/moves.ts`, `src/director/film.ts`, `src/terrain/cover.ts`)

- Cover windows: dive frames 1876 to 1891, centre 1884 (the view switches from orbit to terrain at the centre); rise 2122 to 2137, centre 2130. The cover is a full-frame pass. Without `coverEdge` the amount is a smooth rise to 1 at the centre and back. With `coverEdge: [first, last]` the amount is min(smooth(x / first), smooth((1 - x) / last)) over the window; the rise uses `coverEdgeRise`. Colours: `cover` and `coverLow` on the orbit side, `coverTerrain` and `coverLowTerrain` on the terrain side; `coverLow` must be set for horizon, `coverTop`, `coverShell`, flow and `coverRush` to apply. Sky exposure is times (1 - amount) squared. To look at the join without the cover set `coverEdge: [1e6, 1e6]` for a still.
- Terrain entry: offset (height `entryHeight` g, back `entryBack` g), g = x^2.2, x from 1 at the cover's first frame to 0 at the end of the dive (g 0.643 at the centre, 0.37 at 1891). Exit: g = (u / 0.5067)^2.2 from frame 2100 (0.243 at 2120, 0.594 at 2130).
- `dive.swoop: true` takes position, heading, pitch and roll at the cover centre from the terrain entry, so the views join; `surge` retimes it. `rise.level: true` carries pitch and heading across the rise cover (the pullback then shows Earth rolled about 52 degrees; `rise.rollDeg` may take part of it back); `settle`, `hug`, `ahead`, `pan`.
- G13: a pixel is soft when texel density is under 1; a frame fails over 2 percent soft; measured at draft on hold, dive, terrain and rise frames outside the cover windows. Patch weight = front x feather 0.12 x (1 - smoothstep(1.02, 1.5, parent density)).
- Mars open items to stay clear of: 6 (rise reads as a concealed cut: streaming cover in the climb, thinning of ten frames or more on the orbit side, terrain sky faded across the pullback) and 7 (dive seems to stop under a blur dissolve: carry the plunge's speed through the first second of the terrain view).

### Fix 1, entry motion (from 07:15 UTC)

- Tool `npx tsx assets-src/earth/dive/canvas.ts --frames A,B [--set JSON] [--scan first,last]`: per frame of the terrain side of the dive, the terrain view and the terrain side of the rise it prints the camera in relief space, its speed, the footprint of the frame on the ground canvas (x of -640 to 3456, bottom ymax of 1980, image px) and the flow in screen px per frame at the bottom, the middle and the left of the frame.
- Cause of the stall. In relief space -z is the optical axis (28.3 degrees below level) and +y the camera's up, so the old entry (height 0.9, back 1) was a 70 degree descent: the whole picture slid up 7 to 12 px per frame and stopped at 1919. `gather: 0.8` made the glide stand still through the whole dive (u stays near -0.31 from 1876 to 1920; the glide's speed is 0.2 of its mean at 1920): flow at the bottom of the frame 0.4 px per frame at 1919, 0.5 at 1920.
- The hard limit is the bottom apron. Forward flight brings new ground in at the bottom of the frame; the canvas holds 396 image px (270 screen px) below the judged frame, so between the first clear frame (about 1888) and 2010 the flow at the bottom edge can average 2.2 px per frame at most. Any entry that flows downward (forward) costs bottom apron; a descent flows upward and costs the sides (limit about 1.4 times at 1888).
- Measured options (bottom, middle flow in px per frame): pure glide run back through the dive, `entryHeight 0, entryBack 0`: gather 0.4 gives 1.1, 0.5 at 1886 and 1.5, 0.6 at 1920 with ymax 2002 at 1886, 1981 at 1894, 1904 at 1920; gather 0.5 gives 0.8 to 1.2, ymax 1954 to 1881; gather 0.3 gives 1.4 to 1.7, ymax 1928 at 1920. Any descent on top (`entryHeight` 0.1 and more) turns the flow upward first and brings the reversal (the stall) back near 1910 to 1914.
- A faster plunge after the cover needs more bottom apron (about 300 image px more for twice the speed). The relief margin asset has used 6 of 6 takes in round 1, so that is for round 2.

### The limb of the relief follows the true limb (`relief.ts` `place()`, `look.ground.lock`, from 09:10 UTC)

- Cause of the missing blue line at 2125 to 2127 (and of a horizon that sank too fast in the climb): rays of the fitted camera that miss the sea sphere were put on a wall at the tangent distance (8.13 camera heights), standing on the limb circle of the fitted camera. From a higher camera the true limb lies above that wall's foot (3.9 degrees at 2129), and `coverSea` and the veil cut at the true limb, so the deck covered the blue line. From a camera further back the sea's own bulge hid the wall's foot (about 7 px at 1920).
- Fix: the vertex shader of the ground and tower meshes moves every vertex whose fitted ray is above `lock[1]` (-0.003 rad below the fitted limb) in elevation only, in the vertical plane through the camera's nadir axis, so that its angle above the true limb of the current camera equals its angle above the limb in the approved image. Between `lock[0]` (-0.014 rad) and `lock[1]` the vertex is a mix of its place on the sea and the locked place, so that strip of haze under the limb stretches when the camera climbs. Sideways the vertex keeps the parallax of a point at the tangent distance. At the fitted pose (frame 2010) the move is the identity.
- Checked at draft (`out/work/earth/p17/`, sheets `lock-a.jpg`, `lock-b.jpg`, `lock-c.jpg`, `rise-s7.jpg`): 2120, 2124, 2126, 2127 keep a clean blue limb line above the deck (before: a frayed band at 2120, a dark edge with no blue at 2126 and 2127). 2099, 2110, 1920, 1900, 1886: clean limb, no fold, no tear. 2010 against the still before the lock: max 8 code values, 1.6 percent of pixels, all in limb rows 150 to 330 (perspective interpolation with other vertex depths); against the approved close image the frame is marginally closer (limb band mean abs 3.243 after, 3.263 before; whole frame 4.055 after, 4.058 before).

### The rise cut is still a concealed cut (09:25 UTC, own weak list item 1)

- The look lock names it: "a full-frame cover that paints over space beyond the limb" and a cover that "clears onto a limb in two frames" read as a concealed cut. The whole frame veil of 5ed4c0e is that (white at 2129 to 2131, open at 2133). It hides two real breaks: the limb jumps about 190 px at the cut and the Sun is in frame only on the terrain side.
- Cause of the limb jump, from `src/director/moves.ts`: on the orbit side `climb()` holds the limb at `carried = horizonDeg - exitPitchDeg * g` above the axis and adds the true dip of the globe. On the terrain side the camera only pitches by `exitPitchDeg * g`, but it also climbs (`exitHeight` 2.3), so the true limb sinks by the growth of the dip (14.0 to about 21.7 degrees at 2129). The difference is that growth, whatever `exitPitchDeg` is. Mars climbs 0.8 heights over a sphere that is far larger against the camera height, so its dip hardly grows.
- Cause of the Sun pop (`npx tsx assets-src/earth/sunat.ts`): at 2010 the Sun is 27.4 degrees above the axis (y 1.251, the frame edge is 1), at 2099 y 1.118; the exit pitch of 11 degrees brings it into frame from about 2116 (2120 y 0.949, 2129 y 0.774); at 2130 it is at y 2.76.
- Plan: (a) ask for `terrain.exitDipDeg` (default 0): `carried` minus that angle, so the orbit side starts with the limb where the climbed terrain camera has it; (b) `exitPitchDeg` at or below 0 so the Sun never enters the frame; (c) the veil stays below the limb and `look.veil.whole` goes to 0.

### Outside the hold: `away`, the far map, the aurora map, the sky margin (10:15 to 10:45 UTC, working tree)

- `away` (`set.ts`): 0 until frame 1800, 1 from 1851 and in the rise (`look.away = [1, 0.7]`, seconds before and after the end of the hold). Every change below is times `away`, so hold frames before 1800 are the same bytes as before (checked: 1755 against p13 differs only in the aurora sector, from the aurora map change below).
- Why: the wrap map is the hero where the hero shows the globe, and the hero's dark side (night and twilight) divided by a dark light curve is amplified noise, with the hero's on disc aurora left in the surface colour (North Atlantic, lon -40 to -5, lat 25 to 65) and in the cloud colour, and the hero's limb pixels stretched. In the hold that is the approved picture. From any other camera it is the faulted material (items 2, 3, 4, 6).
- Cause found for the stretched lights and smeared land past the hero's limb (item 2): the registration flow (`out/work/earth/guide/flow.npy`, hero geography against the real one) is 4 to 10 degrees (max 16) and falls to zero within about 6 degrees past the hero's limb, so the far map there was squeezed and stretched (Europe and its lights in horizontal streaks).
- Fix: a second map `wrap-far.webp` (`wrap.py 8192 far`, 80 s): Blue Marble through the hero colour table as before, but placed with a gentle flow (`far_flow()`: the old flow where the hero is lit and faces the camera, a smooth extension of it elsewhere, fading to zero at 172 degrees from the hero centre; stretch outside the trusted zone 1st to 99th percentile -0.07 to 0.06 along x, -0.17 to 0.09 along y, before -0.6 to 0.9). RGB is the surface, alpha the Black Marble lights (square root coded, 8192 wide, glow 2.2 px, so points). Full 8192 by 4096 (5.2 MB), web 4096 by 2048 (1.2 MB).
- Shader (`globe.ts`, all inside `for (k < (uAway > 0 ? 1 : 0))`): `bad = away * (1 - smoothstep(far.light, held - cap))` where `held` is the light of the hero at that place and `cap` widens the zone around the aurora residue (`far.cap`: lon, lat, boost, inner and outer radius in degrees); surface mixes to the far map by `bad`; cloud colour goes neutral by `bad` (green tint of the hero's aurora over cloud); lights mix to the far lights by `rim` (`far.rim` on the cosine from the hero centre: the hero's limb lights are stretched). Night flatten as before but the tone is a mix of a sea tone and a land tone by the red to blue ratio of the surface, so night land reads.
- Aurora map: red glow cleaned (see above in the summary of 10:15), on disc aurora times `1 - away`.
- Sky patch margin: with a low pass margin the dive showed a starless strip about 140 px wide at the left frame edge (1840, 1857, `/tmp/sky-edges.png` pushed as a look). The engine mixes patch and shared sky by one weight, so a starless margin dims the shared stars too. Now the margin is the low pass plus the star points of the padded image turned (side margins flipped top to bottom, top and bottom margins flipped left to right, corners both): no mirror line at the approved border, stars continue. Inside the approved border nothing changes.

### Sky margin at 1857: a starless strip (found 12:27 UTC on the 1857 final, top left)

- At 1857 the left 150 px of the frame are the margin of the hold sky patch. It read as a smooth hazy strip with few stars and a vertical edge against the hero's Milky Way (`/tmp/s2.png`; the round 11 frame had the mirrored copy there). Cause: the margin's star points were flipped top to bottom, so the top left got the star poor bottom left.
- Fix in `sky/patch.py` `save()`: points = image minus its 4 px low envelope (`FINE`), moved outward by 1.8 margin widths along the row for the side margins and along the column for top and bottom (`SHIFT` 0.8 = the source strip starts 0.8 margins inside the border); a star above 0.2 linear (`PEAK`, the top 2.5 percent; star peaks: median 0.008, 90th 0.042, 97th 0.16, 99th 0.52) is scaled down to it within 8 px (`REACH`), so no bright star shows twice; fade in over 4 px from the border (`JOIN`).
- First take (points above the 12 px envelope, peaks clipped at 0.12): clipped stars became flat blobs and copied Milky Way clouds were cut at the border (`out/work/earth/skytry/tl.jpg`). Dropped.
- Second take (`out/work/earth/skytry/tl2.jpg`, old left, new right; dropped later, see the next section): the margin is a field of fine stars at the density of the sky beside it (share over 60 code values 0.0064 against 0.0074 beside it; before 0.0048). Inside the approved border 0 pixels differ from the shipped file. Sizes: full 5.82 MB (5.75), web 1.68 MB (1.66).
- `EARTH_SKY_OUT=DIR python3 assets-src/earth/sky/patch.py out/work/earth/still/hold-nosky.png` writes to `DIR/full` and `DIR/web` instead of `public` (for a try while a render queue runs). Run takes 100 s.
- Done in the next section: copy the two files into `public/assets/earth/{full,web}/`, build, draft 1755 (must equal p37 inside the border), 1840 and 1857 (`mirrorcheck.py`), commit.
- Planned then, replaced by the `ground` change of the next section: `look.globe.away.landAt[2]` 0.28 to 0.2. At 2156 final the night land median is (14, 14, 20), 10th to 90th percentile of the mean 11 to 31, against the sea (4, 13, 27); with the flat tone before it was (21, 21, 28). A reference of 0.2 puts the median near 17 and keeps the light and dark.

### Rise: ease out without the stop and restart (designed 14:50 UTC, not applied yet)

- Now (`npx tsx assets-src/earth/dive/ease.ts --kind rise --step 1`): the rate per frame falls with a ratio that steepens from 0.95 (2138) to 0.55 (2156), is 0.00 from 2160 to 2162 and comes back to -0.05 (the drift into the travel). A brake to a dead stop and a restart. Mercury and Neptune have the same curve and R4 faulted both (\"abrupt deceleration to a near-complete stop\", \"lengthen the ease-out curve\").
- Cause of the stop: `StopPlan.rise` blends its path into `after(time)` over the last 40 percent, and the settle (10, gentle) has brought the path to rest before the drift has weight.
- Round 11 faulted the smeared sky of 2156 (settle 5). That smear was the camera's turn, not its travel: stars do not move when the camera only recedes.
- Design: `EarthPlan extends StopPlan`, `override rise` scales the camera position of `super.rise` by exp(-gain s^a (1 - s)^b), s from `tail.from` of the segment to its end. The direction from the planet and the camera's turn stay as they are, so the planet's centre stays on its screen point, the stars are as sharp as now, and the last frame is the same pose with the same speed (end gap 8e-8, speed 8.000e-2).
- `npx tsx assets-src/earth/dive/tail.ts [--first FRAME] [--tail JSON]` prints rate, ratio and blur per frame, now and with the tail. `{from 0.5467, gain 3.5, shape [2, 6.5]}`: ratio 0.87 to 0.78 from 2141 to 2163, no stop; 2156 -0.41 percent per frame, body blur median 0.7 px, p90 1.0 (now 0.2 and 0.4; 1857 has 0.9). Gain 5.2: ratio 0.80 to 0.85, 2156 -0.56, blur 1.0 and 1.3. Limb radius px 2142, 2149, 2156, 2163: now 642, 415, 389, 389; gain 3.5: 645, 429, 395, 389; gain 5.2: 646, 437, 398, 390.

### 1857 cloud fringes: cause found in `globe.ts` (01:36 to 01:45 UTC, measure still running)

- Item 8, "stretched cloud striations near the limb at 1857 with oversharpened fringes": the 1857 pose is only 1.7 deg from the hold's direction (eye distance 3.745 against 4.442), so the limb at 1857 is the hero's own limb at 1.17 times the size. Crops of the kept final still (`out/work/earth/p6/limb1857-south.png`, `limb1857-hero-film.png` hero above film, `limb1857-nn.png` 10 times nearest): the lit clouds are covered with 2 to 3 px parallelograms in white, cyan and pink that the hero does not have, across the whole cloud field and not only at the limb.
- Cause: outside the hold the cloud is multiplied by `1 + uAway * fine[0] 0.6 * (far cloud alpha minus its own low pass)` while it is still tone coded and premultiplied. The scaled coded value then goes through `inverseFilmic` (a coded 0.8 times 1.18 is far over the shoulder, per channel, hence the white and cyan dots) and the alpha can pass 1, which gives the surface a negative weight (the pink). At the hold `uAway` is 0, so 1755 never showed it.
- Fix, in the worktree (`globe.ts`, `tsc` passes, not rendered): the fine term is a factor `more` on the cloud's coverage in scene light: `a = cloud.a * more`, colour `inverseFilmic(cloud.rgb) * more`, `more` capped at `1 / cloud.a`. The cloud's own colour stays, the alpha stays within 1. `fine[0]` unchanged. 1755 and 2010 keep their bytes (the loop does not run at `uAway` 0).
- Moon generation prompt saved as `assets-src/earth/moon-prompt.txt` for the recipe.
- Queue scripts ready: `out/work/earth/p6/qa.sh` (final stills 1857, 2156, terrain sheet at review, final stills 1755, 2010, into `out/work/earth/p6/qa/`), `out/work/earth/p6/pb-assets.sh` (applies `all.patch`, runs `air.py --under`, `aurora.py`, `moon.py`, `relief/low.py`, build).

In set.ts `born = smooth(...)` multiplies the gain of the air shell's aurora and `uAuroraColor` of the globe (the glow on the disc); aurora.ts scales `uAuroraSpan.z, .w` (low, top) by `1 - (1 - 0.6) * (1 - born)`, so the rays grow to their height while they brighten. From frame 1716 on every uniform has its old value exactly (times 1, minus 0).

- Why (`pb/k4/flow.ts`, the plan's own poses): the rush pattern runs outward at `speed k.z / k.y` per second in log radius: 1.75 (fine) and 2.67 (billow) at speed 2.4, that is 6 and 9 percent of the radius per frame. The world under the camera grows at speed over height: dive orbit side 4 per second at 1877, 8 (1879), 15 (1880), 27 (1881), 31 (1882), 10 (1883), so 27 to 100 percent of the radius per frame; rise orbit side 12 (2131), 19, 19, 13, 10, 8, 6 (2137). On the terrain sides the camera is slow (rise 1.7 to 2 per second at 2120 to 2129, dive nearly at rest from 1885). So 2.4 fits the terrain sides and is 5 to 10 times too slow for the plunge: near the centre the fan of rays is the same picture for five frames. The phase is 0 at the centre for any speed, so only the rate per frame counts: `speed k.z / 30` of a noise cell.
- The speed also moves where the cover opens (its alpha reads the same noise): at 2132 and 2133 the deck with speed 8 hides the globe where 2.4 shows it through holes. So every cover frame has to be looked at for any new speed.

## 08:17 to 08:35 UTC: E1 merged, S3, the path

Rise: `at 0.005` (the engine wants `at` above 0), T at 2100.25, place window 2100 to 2112. So all 90 frames of the dive and all 75 of the rise are the globe side; the frame of T is half and half through the shutter, at the twin.
- **Close side on dive and rise**: the level glide of the terrain view carried on in time, `terrain(time - terrain.start)`. The old entry and exit terms and the cover values are gone from `params`.
- **Globe side** (`plan.ts`, values in `place.json` block `path`): anchor = `twin(glide(t), t)`. Height = anchor height times exp(L(x)), x frames from T. L comes from `law(frames, ease, total, last)`: the rate is 0 at T, eases over `ease[0]` frames to a constant, and over `ease[1]` frames into `last`, the hold's own rate for the dive and the travel's for the rise; `total` is ln(far height / anchor height). With k = L / total: nadir = slerp(anchor nadir, far direction) over `over`, aim = lerp(P, far aim) over `aim`, up = slerp(anchor up, far up) over `turn`, vfov by k, each with a quintic ease; orientation by `lookAt`. P is where the anchor's optical axis meets the unit sphere.
- **Clock**: the spin rewind of 11.5 s (12.65 degrees), a jump at the cover centre before, is now `time - 11.5 * smooth(ramp(T + rewind / fps, rise.end, time))`: equal to `time` through frame 2100 and to `time - 11.5` from 2175, so hold, terrain and travel see the states they saw.
- **Veil**: `veil.ts`, `look.veil` and all its wiring in `set.ts` removed. "After the rise" in `set.ts` is now `time > handoverOf('earth', 'rise').time` instead of a comparison of `clock(time)` with `time`.

The shader adds `(near - inside * laid) * tone` in display code values, `laid` the share of the pixel that comes from any level, so the footprint shows G minus the grade while the camera is high and G itself when it is low. ## 12:41 to 13:20 UTC: the cloud field as bodies, the calm, the wipes, the hold under the field (MAIL 254, 2 to 4; MAIL 259, 5 and 6)

- `deck.py` cuts the four takes into bodies (matte by the darkest channel against the local top, cast shadow map from the lit sea round each body, turned so the shadows fall the way the Sun of the place throws them) and lays them out on a grid with a seeded shuffle over 24 degrees about P (8192 px), each body kept or dropped by the density under it. Output `field-alpha.npy`, `field-colour.npy`, `field-shade.npy`, `field-density.png` in `out/work/earth/place/`. `deck-3.log`: cover of the takes 0.194, 0.171, 0.203, 0.195; 57 of 90 spots placed; cover where the density is over 0.9: 0.434. The first layout was too dense and grey (cover 0.761); `step` 0.55, `density.full` 0.8, `shadow.onCloud` 0.25 since.
- Density: the cloud of the ring take outside the plate, the plate's own far cloud inside it (from 5.0 to 6.4 degrees from the nadir).
- `levels.py` rewritten. The field is laid over every level, the plate and the fine level, so a cloud mass ends in bodies and the bodies throw shadows on the sea. The plate gives way to the hold's own levels (12 where it reaches, 24 beyond, through `seaGain`) by the density and by the far ramp; the far zone of the plate was a repaint with dots and streak blobs. The old composite of the ring sheet is gone.
- `calm.py`: the dot pattern on land (reads as lights by day). Opening by a disc, then a median, on land only (green or pale ground near, warmer than the sea, away from cloud wider than the disc). A parameter named `r` clashed with the red channel in the first version; renamed `dot`.
- Wipes (`mend.json` `wipe`): marks of the repaint in the plate, painted over from their surround.
- `globe.ts`: uniform `uLowSize`, so the texel measure counts the low plate's own density where the low look shows. The `tuned()` hook is out of `place.ts` and `set.ts`.
- First test frames (draft, `out/work/earth/place/m3/`): the field over the Gulf and Yucatan reads as bodies with shadows and ends in bodies; the far bank at the top of 1890 and 1900 has cumulus detail. Wrong: field bodies outside the low plate read pink to mauve in the top corners of 1890, 1900, 2124, 2129; two soft white wedges at 1890 and 1900; the cream patch of the glint.
- The mauve, cause: the tone texture (what the plate's sea differs from the hold's by) was added on the grey flanks of clouds; its cloud gate looked at the darkest channel only. Fix: the tone also needs colour, `plates.tone.grey` [0.2, 0.45] (spread of the three channels over the brightest), uniform `uToneGrey`. After it the corners of 1890, 1900, 2124 and 2129 are white and grey.
- The wedges, cause: two marks of the repaint in the plate at plate px (3020, 2168) and (3121, 2031); the disc of the wipe was smaller than the mark, so the fill started from the mark's own rim. The wipe now takes everything brighter than `bright` inside `reach` times the radius, grown by `growPx`.

## MAIL 304 from the Builder to mercury_builder and earth_builder (16:57 UTC, high priority; verbatim)

From handover_engineer, on why the globe alone differs from the place picture by 13 to 15.5 levels at your handovers (limit 6, a warning) and what shows of it. His words:
"Part is a setting, part can be the engine, the rest is plates. Setting: neither Mercury nor Earth sets edgeIn (on main since 0eae595). Mercury's four sided outline at 738 to 741 is the picture's valid rectangle with the film's narrow feather; with edgeIn (Mars uses 0.4, 0.4, 0.4, 0.25) the sides become a ramp that reaches in while the weight is low and draws back by T. Engine: a tone difference shows as an outline or an island because the picture brings its broad tone and its detail in with one weight. I can split the two: the detail keeps today's weight and edges, the broad tone of the picture is led over to the tone of the plates toward the picture's rim while the weight is under 1, and the correction is zero at T. Off unless a stop asks. It can not make the tone change inside the window smaller, only take its edge away: at T the picture has its own tone over the whole frame, so plates 15 levels off still turn the frame within 12 frames. Mercury's far field going pale and flat from 993: its rise sets maxEnlarge 1.2, which cuts the picture there, so that is the plates alone showing (or the rise path: on Mars fromDive made the cut needless)."

## 16:00 to 18:10 UTC: the glint cure, the veil of the low plate, the numbers for round 40, the shutter trial

The glint cure (MAIL 297, first). The cream patch south of Cuba in 1860 to 1876 was the plate's sun glint: the plate is the look from the close camera, which looks into the Sun's reflection, and the globe showed that reflection from straight above, where no camera would see it. Cure: `levels.py` (`glint_of`) measures the glint on the plate, works out the calm sea under it (`place-glint-sea.png`) and the glint's light (`place-glint-light.png`), and the globe takes the light off the plate per pixel where the ray from the ground to the camera is `plates.glint.seenDeg[0]` (45) degrees or more from the ray to the close camera; the whole glint shows from `seenDeg[1]` (15). Trials as the looks notes hold them: trial 1 turned the cream to mint, not taken; trials 2 and 3 rejected; trial 5 (the plate without its glint by view angle) took the patch off in 1860 to 1876 but left clouds over the glint and a red tail wrong; trial 6 (the one in the tree) takes the measured light off per pixel and keeps the clouds. glint7 was trial 6 with the low plate's angle changed, for the level step. Seen on draft frames: the cream patch is gone in 1860 to 1876 and the glint comes in over 1880 to 1892; at half strength (1884) it is a muted brown, on the list. Texture memory of the stop 1394 MB (limit 1400).

The level step of the rise (MAIL 297, second). Measured with `out/work/earth/place/tmp/lev.py` (whole frame mean luma and mean colour of consecutive draft frames, the same quantity as the tool's level step), frames 2113 to 2146:

| glint cure alone (glint7) | 8.15 into 2124 | 8.92 into 2124 |
| veil1 | 5.10 into 2124 | 5.79 into 2124 |
| veil2 | 5.36 into 2126 | 6.00 into 2125 |

## 23:50 to 00:20 UTC, step 3 trials b4 to b7: one share for the whole close world, and what the far cap shows

- b4: the towers write their own depth range (gl_FragDepth = gl_FragCoord.z times towers.range), so they never fight the sea or the globe; the far sheet is held at the sea (min of 1); the texel footprint is capped (long axis at most towers.stretch times the short one). Frame 2010 against step 1 (46fe41ce), draft tier: mean 0.003, largest 2 code values.
- b5: the close world is laid under the globe front to back. First the sea sheet takes the globe's light down by the share the place has at that point (colour times 1 minus share, alpha set to 0), then front cap, far cap and sea are added in that order, each times 1 minus the alpha already there. So the globe keeps 1 minus share and the close world, composed as in the surface view, gets the share. In the surface view the share is 1 and the order and blend are the usual over. Frame 2010 against step 1: mean 0.003, largest 2.
- What that showed on frames (looks pushed 00:05, 1da104dc): in step 1 a tower in front of the glint turned pale at 2118 (the sea's glint came through it by share times 1 minus share); with b5 the towers at 2118 have the tone they have at 2099 and 2106. So the difference of b5 against step 1 at 2118 (mean 0.99) is this cure, not a darker tower. Still to measure on a tracked tower.
- The lone dark pixels on rims at 2118 stayed in b5. Diagnosis with a debug switch (not committed), frame 2118, pixels round (675, 400) and (683, 417): no towers 223 to 225 (glint); front cap alone 192 to 225; far cap alone 157 to 190 where it shows; all 152 to 180 on a line one or two pixels wide. The far cap carried the picture's texels, which under a lit rim are the blue shade of the near face, and from a camera above the plate camera it shows past the top rim: a dark line outside a lit rim. Raising towers.cut to 0.96 (b6) made the line wider (the far cap then shows through the near cap's fringe) and moved 2010 by up to 20, so cut is back at 0.5.
- b7: the far cap is the side of the body the plate camera never saw. It gets its light from the scene's Sun: where its outward normal (from the mesh, away from the plate camera) turns to the Sun (towers.face, cosine from 0 to 0.5) it shows the lit tone of the towers (towers.lit: the mean colour of the brightest tenth of the closed texels of the tower texture, measured by body.py), elsewhere the picture's shade. The near cap stays the picture as painted. The Sun comes from plan.lightDir carried into the place frame (place.ts carry), the same on both sides of T.
- Decision (c) of mail 398: bodies do not shade one another. Each near cap carries the painted light, which already holds the shade its neighbours throw; a second cast would darken twice.
- Shadow direction measure (assets-src/earth/relief/shadow.py): for each body over 1500 px with a shadow found at its foot, the line on the sea from the foot that is darkest against the lines 20 degrees to either side, against the direction the scene Sun casts. 12 of 15 bodies. ## Note 501 from the Builder, received 03:38 UTC (verbatim)

NOTE 501 to every stop builder and globe_engineer, from the Builder, 03:38 UTC. A fault of the whole film, found by the first whole smooth report from the machines (Mercury, job 14): the same film frame at uhd is not the same picture as at 16 by 9 (one block differs by 45.8 levels at 713, limit 12).
CAUSE, found by mercury_builder: every globe brings its plate levels and its fine levels in by the texels of the parent a pixel of the format (uPatchFade 1.1 to 1.7 against gd * scale * size, gd from dFdx and dFdy). At uhd a pixel is half as large, so every level comes in at twice the height; at preview at half the height; in the live player it depends on the window. Brandon captures at uhd, so he gets another film than the one we judge. The term is in src/bodies/planet.ts (globe_engineer) and in the own globe code of mercury, venus, earth, jupiter, uranus, neptune and the Sun (src/stops/&lt;stop&gt;/globe.ts or planet.ts).
RULING (plan F: whatever blends does so by distance, height or angle): the measure is texels of the parent a 1080th of the frame height, an angle, not a pixel. In practice one factor, the height of the drawing buffer in pixels over 1080 (1 at 16 by 9, 2 at uhd, 0.5 at preview), multiplied into the density that a fade reads (parent, texels, fine, thin, cap, whatever your code calls it) and into nothing that only picks a mip for sampling.
PROOF, both by you before you name the commit: (a) at 16 by 9 the factor is 1 and every byte stays: the hashes of your own draft frames before and after are equal. (b) at uhd the picture becomes the 16 by 9 picture, only finer: npm run smooth -- --stop ID --only parity on your tree (seven frames), limits mean 12, coarse mean 3.2, one block 12, frame level 2.2.
THE SAME RULE holds for every other number in your stop that is counted in pixels and can be seen: the width of a feather, the radius of a glow, a threshold of a size on screen, a point size. If your parity is still red with the factor in, the panel names the block: find the term.
WHO: each stop builder, in the commit you name next (mercury_builder has it in work). globe_engineer: src/bodies/planet.ts and anything else under src/bodies and src/core that reads a density a pixel, as one commit on newest main (6884e80 or later), then ask me for the engine proof and say which stops draw with the shared code. saturn_coder and mars_place_builder: check your place code for the same kind of term and say what you found.
A red parity is a severe item in a stop's round.

My note on it: it goes into the commit of step 4, after the step's own frames are proved (so the two proofs do not mix): the factor in Earth's own globe code, proof (a) by file hashes of draft frames before and after, proof (b) by the parity part of the smooth harness on the merged tree. ## NOTE 504 from the Builder, 03:51 UTC (verbatim)

NOTE 504 to every stop builder, from the Builder, 03:51 UTC. On NOTE 501 (the factor), two things from globe_engineer that save you a wrong factor:
1. Do NOT take the factor from view.format in the pass that draws a place picture. There view.format is the layout's, larger by the picture's scale (2 at 16 by 9), so view.format.height over 1080 is 2 at 16 by 9 in that pass and your place picture's bytes change. And the edge limit (handover.place.maxEdge 4800) gives the uhd picture the scale 1, so a pixel of the uhd place picture is a pixel of the master's place picture: there the right factor at uhd is 1, not 2, for code that does not already multiply by uFine. Code that multiplies its density by uFine (the terrain shaders) needs the format's factor alone.
2. The shared helper, in proof now and on main as soon as it is clean (agent/engine-globe, globe_engineer names the commit): src/core/frame.ts with frameUniform (the format's height over the master's, set by the engine in applySize, usable as a uniform), setPass (the engine sets it while a place picture is drawn) and bufferFrame() (the two multiplied, for code that reads a density a pixel of the buffer and knows nothing of uFine).
RULING: use the helper, not a factor of your own. If your cure is already written with your own uniform (uranus_builder: seen.ts), keep working with it and swap its source to the helper when I tell you it is on main; that swap changes no byte and needs no new proof beyond the hashes. If you have not started, fetch globe_engineer's commit when it names it and write against the helper. Stops with no place picture left (plan F) have only case 1's last sentence to mind.

## MAIL 526 from the Builder (/root), 04:52 UTC, word for word

MAIL 526 from the Builder (/root), 04:52 UTC, one mail to every stop builder and to handover_engineer: THE SEAM WITH THE SURFACE VIEW. A ruling (d196).

FOUND on Mars's rise at 60 pictures a second. MEASURED by me on the pictures: the change from picture to picture falls from 5.3 to 2.7 within three capture frames after the seam (film frame 2670) and is at 8.8 four later. The cause, measured by handover_engineer on the path (STATED): the eye's own speed over its own height falls to 0.33 of the surface view's at 2671 + 1/2 and is at 2.2 five capture frames later. The surface view pushes toward its place; the rise pulls back along the line from the place to the eye; so the eye stops and turns back. The path part of `npm run smooth` is green over it, because it reads the picture's speed round the place and not the eye against the near ground. This is a "moment of lag" at the change of view, and it is in the film, not in the player.

THE RULE. Plan E says a dive and a rise meet "the surface view's own move with the same speed and direction". That holds for the frames after the seam as well as at it: across each seam with the surface view the eye's speed over its own height never dips and never turns back. A new line in the path part of `npm run smooth` will read it at all 17 seams (harness_builder, due 05:40 UTC). Its limit is set from a calibration on main and logged before any round uses it.

WHERE IT IS CURED: in the surface view's own path, which is yours. Not in the engine's law: handover_engineer searched the law four times, and every cure there turns the lens more than the turn limit allows in the frames a rise has. STATED by handover_engineer, a scratch on Mars with the surface view's velocity at the seam turned: pulling back up its own line, the rise's lowest speed is 1.05 and it never turns back; across its lens 0.95 and 1.02; 45 degrees off 0.53; pushing at its place 0.33. A dive arrives down the surface view's way (0.98 and more on the one move).

So a surface view is one flight that takes the dive's motion at its first frame and hands the rise its motion at its last. Where yours pushes in, it bends over its last seconds from the push into a track across and on into the pull back, without losing speed (no rest: a rest is a dent of its own) and with the lens turning inside the turn limits. Where yours already pulls back or tracks across at its end, show it with the new line and change nothing.

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: the picture of the judged surface frame. On a finished stop its camera stays to the byte (Sun 0, 60 and 90, Mars 2580, Jupiter 3150, Saturn 3720); on the others the composition of the approved close image at the judged frame stands. The bend lives after the judged frame. On Mars, whose surface view Brandon approved in motion, nothing before frame 2610 changes.

WHO, by handover_engineer's numbers (the eye's lowest speed over the surface view's own, on your own path today unless it says forced): Mars 0.33 (rise), Uranus 0.46 at 4382 (rise), Earth 0.64 at 2116 (rise) and 0.69 at 1905 (dive), Venus 0.78 (dive), Mercury 0.83 at 961 (rise), Sun 0.92 (0.38 forced onto the one move), Jupiter 0.76 forced (its view is nearly still at the seam), Neptune 0.98, Saturn not measured. On Mars the bend goes into mars_place_builder's commit; handover_engineer gives it the numbers.

TIME. The 07:00 UTC point of d186 stands for everything else. ## MAIL 596 from the Builder (/root), about 09:03 UTC, word for word

MAIL 596 from the Builder (/root) to the nine stop builders. A check tool for the pattern number is on main 81d568a7 (globe_engineer's NAMED f65859e1): `assets-src/shared/globe-levels.py`. It lays one level of a plate pyramid against the part of its parent that it covers, both at the state in which the level comes in (a parent texel 0.8 px of the frame), and judges the pair with the smooth report's own `pattern` function and the config's numbers. Seconds, no render. Merge main, or copy that one file to the same path in your tree, then:
python3 assets-src/shared/globe-levels.py --dir public/assets/ID/full --json src/stops/ID/FILE.json [--key levels] [--suffix=-dive] [--pairs 0-1,1-3] [--panel out.png]
or with the levels by hand: --level FILE:WIDTHDEG[:EASTDEG,NORTHDEG] twice or more (a plate given by the tangent of its half width: WIDTHDEG = 2 atan of it). One line a pair, OVER and exit 1 above smooth.pictures.maxPattern. It reads files, not the shader: a pair is a test only when both files are the same kind of picture (colour with colour, light with light), and it knows nothing of what a stop does with a level by height.

MEASURED by me on main's Mars (the old plates): 0.06, 0.00, 0.06, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00 in 3.5 s, as its author states. MEASURED by globe_engineer on the proof trees of the first named commits (not checked by me), 99th percentile against 0.45:
- Mars b83618ec: patch-19 to land-8p5 1.19 OVER, land-3p8 to land-1p6 0.69 OVER, land-1p6 to land-0p7 0.59 OVER, land-0p7 to land-0p3 0.98 OVER; the other three pairs 0.00 to 0.09. In the panel of the first pair the parent shows a bright mound with a crater where the child shows a dark plain with the canyon crack.
- Mercury 9b5f55cd: patch-1 to patch-2 1.09 OVER (dive), patch-2 to patch-3r 0.70 OVER (rise), the others 0.01 to 0.02.
- Uranus 9a369939: every pair 0.00 to 0.01. Its red is not in the plates.
- Venus 3b52b0eb: colour 0.01 and 0.02; light a to b 0.20 and 0.13; light b to d 1.12 and 1.10 OVER, with a caution (the two light plates may not be the same quantity).
- Not run: Saturn, Jupiter, Earth, Neptune, the Sun.

RULED. Where a pair is over, two levels show two different pictures of the same ground, the red pattern number of that move is true, and no exchange by height, however slow, cures it (plan F: one place). The cure is in the files: a level is made from the level under it, or both from one source, so that reduced to its parent's scale it is its parent. Where every pair is clean and the move is still red, the cause is in what the shader adds by height or angle (a second look mixed in, a function layer, a light term), and the same rule holds there: one ground, one law of light, borders set on the ground. No limit moves.

Asked of each of you: run it now on every pyramid your dive and rise show (both sets where they differ) and put its lines into your next NAMED mail. A pair over the limit is named there as red, with its cure. This changes no due time.

## What of Earth still reads the time inside the dive or the rise (for MAIL 613)

Read in `set.ts` on the tree of the second commit:

- `handover.dive` and `handover.rise` of `place.json`: `placeFrames` 0 (no place picture: the plates are the globe's own ground), `skyFrames` 120, `dissolveFrames` 1. The sky weights are Earth's own, by the eye's height (`sky.low` 0.034 to 3.3 on a log scale); `skyWeights` divides the engine's share by time out again, so the 120 frames only keep that share off 0 and 1 inside the moves and do not shape the picture. The hooks `skyFrames: 0`, `plan.eyeHeight`, `plan.air(height)`, `Relief.presence(share)` are on a newer main than the one this commit stands on (09d64d78) and are not used yet.
- Read again at 10:03 in `src/core/engine.ts` (line 341) and `src/director/film.ts` (lines 806 to 827) of main 09d64d78: the weight of a sky patch is the engine's share times the patch's own `weight(time)`. Earth's two patches give `high / (1 - share)` (the hold's patch) and `(1 - high) / share` (the close view's patch), `high` by the eye's height, so the product is `high` and `1 - high` in a dive and `1 - high` in a rise (the hold's patch is not drawn in a rise; the film's own stars stand behind). The engine's share by time is also read for the sky glow (`light.terrainSkyGlow`), the sky's light near the ground (`light.skyLow`), the sky floor and the horizon of a place picture: Earth sets none of the four (`plan.ts` line 24, no `skyFloor`, no `limbSky`), so they do nothing here.
- The carry of the sky (how far the frame of the stars has turned from the globe view's to the close view's) is the engine's `skyTurnWeight(segment, time)`: by the clock over the whole dive and the whole rise, on every stop that does not give `skyCarryShare`. Earth does not give it. It is a turn of the stars' frame, not a fade, and it runs in 1830 to 1919 and 2100 to 2174. Named for MAIL 613; the cure is `skyCarryShare` by the eye's height in `plan.ts`, proved on the frames with stars in them.
- `away` (the globe's look from the hold's to the near one, and the aurora's `uAway`, `uFree`): in the rise by nearness (`look.back` 1.03 to 1.35), in the dive by the time since the end of the hold over `look.away` 0 to 0.85 s. That is frames 1830 to 1855. RED for MAIL 613, not cured in this commit. Cure: the dive takes the law the rise has (nearness), with its own pair of values so that the frames keep their look, proved on 1830 to 1860.
- `flow` (the drift of the clouds eases out before the hold's end and before the rise's end), `plan.clock`, `plan.spin`, the Moon: clouds and bodies in their own time, not meant by the mail.
- `born` and `gone`: the aurora's onset in the hold and its ebb after the end of the rise; outside the two moves.
- The ground and the veil: by height and by slant only. The plate: by height (`uPlaceIn`), the levels by texel density.

- Why the top end reads red, from the measure's own definition (1 less the correlation of the detail of two frames 8 apart): where one picture is flat and the other has strong detail, the first few hundredths of the weight turn the detail of the mix from the one to the other. With s the ratio of the two pictures' detail there, the mix's detail turns by the angle atan(s w / (1 - w)), and the measure reads 1 less the cosine of how far that angle goes in 8 frames. Fitted on v1's own readings: s about 26 at the dive's centre (0.64 at 1868 with the weight going 0 to 0.09), 9 to 15 in the rise, about 10 the other way at the left edge at 2122. So a law that starts from nothing as a square (the smooth step) turns the flat places over within a few frames however slowly the rest goes. What the measure asks for is a weight that grows by the same factor every frame at the top end, and the same for 1 less the weight at the bottom end: an S curve in the log of the height with power law tails.
- MEASURED on v1, the level's step in place over the weight's step, by height (`/tmp/gl/s14/law4.py` holds the table): about -35 at height 0.04, 0 at 0.065, 21 at 0.095, 48 at 0.14, 68 at 0.21, 92 at 0.31, 127 at 0.47 in the rise; the dive the same within a fifth. A unit of weight weighs more from higher up, because more of the frame is the far, pale part of the lay back. So for an even step of light the weight has to go slowly high up and may go faster low down.
- The law for v2: weight = (f(h) - f(top)) / (f(bottom) - f(top)), f(h) = 1 / (1 + (h / mid)^power), h held between bottom and top. Numbers: top 1.3, bottom 0.034, mid 0.09, power 2 (`plates.low.height`, `plates.low.mid`, `plates.low.power`; computed in `set.ts`). It reads the eye's height and nothing else. MAIL 818 from the Builder (/root) to earth_builder, 00:17 UTC by my date -u.

1. NAMED d00366598a0f0e83b0e47f6a8671cabe3355b9b3 is read and your ten pictures are filed (work/p6/eb-d003). I looked at judged-1857, pair-2175 and sg-sizes-1866. In front of them in the queue stand the take check of batch 5 and Mars's new commit; no machine is idle.

2. Ruling on your question (the mip choice of the picture reads, textureGrad in globe.ts and relief.ts). No, a plain filtered read of a picture does NOT go through the frame factor. At 3840 by 2160 the read takes the finer level, and that finer level is what the capture is made for. The frame law (d253) is about choices: everything that decides WHAT is drawn or WHEN it changes (a level, a patch, an exchange, a feather width, a threshold, a count of octaves, a weight computed from texels per pixel or from the length of a gradient) goes through the factor. A filter's footprint is not such a choice.
The test that follows from it: 3840 reduced by 2 against 1920 may differ only as two filters of the same picture differ. A linear read keeps the local mean. So a local mean that differs by 7.91 at 1866 is not the filter, it is something that is not linear after the read, or a choice still steered by the real pixel. Find it by cause at that place before you change anything: (a) a curve, a threshold or a clamp applied to the read value before it is mixed (lights, foam, cloud edge, a mask made from the map); (b) an alpha or a mask that is not premultiplied in the levels of the map; (c) a height or a normal read at a coarser level and then lit; (d) a mix weight that comes from the gradient itself (a level picked from the gradient's length and blended by hand is a choice and goes through the factor). Say which it is with the two stills and the difference picture, and cure that in the K4 commit.

3. K4: your plan and first picture are due 00:30 as set. MAIL 811 (b) and (c), the smear at 1857 and 2156, still wait for my shutter ruling; do not change them meanwhile.

4. Seen in judged-1857: on your commit the camera is far closer at 1857 than on the kept still (the dive's path was retimed on purpose). Noted as meant. The finals of 1857 and 2156 are not asked from you; they are drawn at the take.

### 04:53 mail from handover_engineer (verbatim), received 04:55 by my clock

From handover_engineer, 04:53 UTC, on your ask for the footprint by each pixel's own way. TAKEN. Not built yet; the contract so that you can prepare your callers:

1. `float gradAt(vec3 world)`, in a chunk `GRAD_GLSL` exported from src/diagnostics/diag.ts beside DIAG_GLSL. `world` is the point as three.js has it in world space in the sample being drawn: `(modelMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0)).xyz` of a mesh under your set's `world` (or `over`). The engine keeps the lens at the origin, so it is the vector from the lens to the point in the film's axes. A varying from the vertex shader, or lens ray times distance: both do.
2. The chunk declares `uniform float uGrad;` and its own uniforms itself: take your own `uniform float uGrad;` line out where you put the chunk in, and spread the uniforms I export (one object, in place of `uGrad: gradUniform`). Names in the NAMED mail.
3. The rule is the one you wrote: count = samples / max(seenHere, 1) / cover, never above samples; factor = max(1 / sqrt(max(count, 1)), floor), with soft. seenHere is the way of the point across the open (capped) shutter in px of the master, the measure of rawMotion in src/core/motion.ts.
4. The point is taken as fixed on your body's turning surface on the globe side (the set's frame with the turn of the dive and rise) and fixed in the close set's frame on the close side. The Moon is not on that surface: for moon.ts the way is off by the turn across the shutter, 0.6 px at most at your 1.1 degrees a second; it is yours to call it there or to stay on uGrad.

The cause, read in the code (not yet proved on frames): the plate's sea is (level less tone) times the air's gain by the length, plus the path share times what the level's own sea differs from that, and the plate's glint is taken off by the seen angle (glint.seenDeg). The ground's sea is the texel times the air's gain over seaGain with no share on its residue, and the ground has no glint law at all. With e = level - (level - tone) seaGain, the ground stands e (gain / seaGain - share) over the plate plus the whole glint. On the shipped level (1024 px, sea texels): level's sea mean (R G B of 255) 23.3 64.4 82.3, (level - tone) seaGain 16.3 55.8 72.7, e mean 7.1 8.4 9.5, mean of its absolute value 9.5 16.9 16.5. The same kind of cause as Venus's (MAIL 1272 item 3): a picture that comes in whole by one law while the plate under it holds a part share by another.

The cure, written as /tmp/gl/k18/patch-relief.py (applied when the bake ends): relief.ts thin() takes the plate's own law for the ground's texel: the glint's light off by the same seen angle (the globe's own uniforms), and the residue e by the same path share, inside the plate's raster with the plate's own feather. No clock and no camera height; at the close pose (share 1, veil gone, angle 0) the texel is the picture as it is, so the surface view and the handover do not change by it.

### The far band by the air path alone (E5), design (03:45 to 03:55 UTC)

What E3 taught, from its two strips and the path numbers of /tmp/gl/k22/dive.json, rise.json (out/work/earth/place/tmp/far5.ts):
1. The reading is largest where the deck's presence passes the middle (rise 2121 against 2129, presence by my count 0.80 to 0.42 at 10 degrees ahead; dive 1888 against 1896, 0.37 to 0.83 at 12 degrees), not where it starts or ends. Two pictures of like strength turn the pattern most in the middle of the swap.
2. So the cure is an even run over as many frames as the geometry gives, without a steep part. In E3 the presence by distance (0.44 at 1870, 1.00 at 1890 at 10 degrees) was multiplied by the air's share, and the product ran steep where both ran.
3. The path (the eye's air mass less one over the close camera's less one) doubles about every 8 frames on the dive (10 degrees ahead: 0.038 at 1868, 0.078 at 1876, 0.158 at 1884, 0.324 at 1892, 0.601 at 1900) and halves about every 10 on the rise (0.585 at 2112, 0.367 at 2120, 0.201 at 2128, 0.104 at 2136, 0.052 at 2144). A presence that is even in the logarithm of the path is therefore even in the frames.
4. The path of every far point is small at the hold and at both judged frames of the moves: at 1755 at most 0.007, at 1857 at most 0.022 (6.5 degrees) and 0.028 (5 degrees), at 2156 at most 0.0233 (6.5 degrees) and 0.028 (5 degrees) (/tmp/gl/k22/early.json, late.json). The reader divides each picture's detail by its local contrast, so the map's pattern stays the reader's pattern until the deck's presence is high (about 0.85), and then the swap of the pattern runs inside the last fifth of the law, which E5 crosses in under 8 frames (0.8 to 1.0 in one doubling of the path, with the eased end). A law that is even in the presence is steep in the odds of the presence at both ends. The cure to try: even in the logarithm of the odds, presence = u^n / (1 + u^n) with u the path over a middle value, so that no ratio of contrasts finds a steep part.

How a swap reads, worked out: with the level's detail a times A and the ground's b times B (A and B not alike), the reader's number over 8 frames is 1 minus the cosine of the change of the angle atan(b / a). A change of gain alone reads nothing. A linear mix by a share w turns that angle fast where A is much stronger than B (a white cloud against haze): the angle stands near zero until w is about 0.8 and then turns through in the last few frames. A share whose odds w / (1 - w) grow at one rate turns the angle at one pace for every strength.
